rounds.text: The business is undergoing a powerful fundamental turnaround in its sales velocity, evidenced by a dramatic acceleration in trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth to 46% [E14], backed by a screen reason highlighting strong sales growth [E42] and a 22% YoY sales increase [E41]. This top-line momentum is directly translating into significant structural margin expansion, with the TTM operating margin surging to 11% from -47% three years prior—an enormous 58 percentage-point improvement [E21]—and reaching an impressive 23% in the quarter ending June 2026 [E22]. Market participants are beginning to recognize this operational inflection, rewarding the stock with steady compounded share price growth of 41% over both the 3-year and 1-year periods [E19, E20], even as the broader results score an exceptional 92 out of 100 pointing to a genuine turnaround that stale sentiment ignores [E45]. Furthermore, profitability metrics show encouraging signs of resilience with net profit up 3% YoY and increasing QoQ [E43, E44], while total borrowings have simultaneously ticked down to Rs 145 Cr [E28]. Conceded: trailing profit growth is negative at -48% [E16] and operating cash flow remains negative at Rs -4 Cr [E26], reflecting near-term cash conversion headwinds [E25].

Binny Mills Ltd carries a prohibitive valuation and severe fundamental risks that are not supported by the evidence, highlighted by a staggering EV/EBITDA of 105.11x against a sector benchmark of just 10.29x [E10]. This excessive multiple is completely detached from the company's long-term top-line stagnation, characterized by a meager 1% compounded sales growth over 10 years and a flagged poor sales growth of 6.84% over the past five years [E11, E37]. Profitability and cash generation remain alarming, with compounded profit growth dropping 40% over 3 years and 48% over the trailing twelve months, alongside negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -4 Cr in Mar 2026 resulting in a weak cash conversion of 0.21x [E15, E16, E26, E27, E25]. Further structural strain is evident in a negative ROA of -11.17%, a negative ROCE of -3.07%, a flagged low interest coverage ratio, and earnings that rely on Rs 1.24 Cr of other income [E7, E9, E36, E38]. Conceded: the company demonstrates positive near-term indicators, including a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 46%, an operating margin reaching 23% in Jun 2026, and a stock price sitting near 95% of its 52-week range [E14, E22, E4].

The bear points to an EV/EBITDA of 105.11x [E10], but this metric fails to capture a fundamental operational turnaround where trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth has surged to 46% [E14] alongside an accelerating sales increase of 22% YoY [E41]. While long-term historical metrics like 10-year sales growth look stagnant at 1% [E11], focusing on them ignores the present reality: operating margins have expanded dramatically to 11% in the TTM from -47% three years earlier (+58 percentage points) and reached 23% in the June 2026 quarter [E21, E22]. Conceded: the company posted negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -4 Cr in March 2026 with a 0.21x cash conversion [E25, E26, E27], and promoter holding has decreased by 5.88 percentage points since December 2023 [E30]. However, dismissing the stock's momentum based on stale historical sentiment is an explicit error according to the turnaround checklist, which notes that current results score 92 out of 100 with net profit up 3% YoY [E43, E45]. Finally, borrowings have decreased slightly to Rs 145 Cr in March 2026 [E28], and compounded share price growth of 41% over the past 1 and 3 years [E19, E20] reflects the market beginning to reprice this dramatic structural improvement rather than a prohibitive valuation.

Conceded: operating margins have expanded dramatically to 11% in TTM and 23% in the June 2026 quarter [E21, E22], and compounded share price growth sits at 41% over the past one and three years [E19, E20]. However, the bull's reliance on a 46% TTM sales surge [E14] glosses over the severe collapse in profitability where compounded profit growth over the same trailing twelve months is -48% alongside a 3-year profit contraction of -40% [E15, E16]. Furthermore, while the bull minimizes negative cash flows, the company actively burned Rs 4 Cr in both operating and free cash flow for March 2026 with a weak 0.21x cash conversion [E25, E26, E27]. The bull also normalizes the massive heavy debt load, but borrowings remain dangerously high at Rs 145 Cr [E28] while the company is officially flagged for a low interest coverage ratio [E36]. While the bull dismisses historical stagnation, long-term 5-year sales growth is flagged as poor at just 6.84% [E37], and earnings are artificially propped up by Rs 1.24 Cr of other income [E38]. Finally, the bull brushes off the insider divestment, yet promoter holding has demonstrably dropped by 5.88 percentage points since December 2023 [E30, E39], signaling that insiders are retreating while expectations run 89% ahead of delivery [E34].
